metas.name: Acre red brick road
metas.note: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Acre small grass hills
metas.note: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Bahia and Pernambuco pole markings
metas.note: Markings on poles are used by the electricity companies to identify them. This pole ID is long, yellow pole paint with a black code. The ones that start with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Carnaúba palms
metas.note: Carnaúba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in Ceará but are also in Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Ceará lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Ceará often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Coffee beans
metas.note: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Concrete bins
metas.note: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and Rondônia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Espírito Santo - Exposed rock
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Goiás pole markings
metas.note: Similar to the Bahia and Pernambuco poles, Goiás poles also use long, yellow pole paint with a black paint code, but it always starts with a number. They also have a rarer yellow on black pole ID, which can be either paint or a plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha
metas.note: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is a Brazilian island with official coverage approximately 340 kilometres northeast of Rio Grande do Norte, and the country itself. It is covered by a white buggy, which is visible at the front. The island is similar in vegetation to the closest part of mainland Brazil, and has large exposed rocks. There is also boat coverage around the island.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Macaw palms
metas.note: Macaw palms have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Maranhão wide insulators
metas.note: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Mato Grosso pole
metas.note: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Paraná pines
metas.note: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Paraná pole markings
metas.note: Pole IDs in Paraná are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Piauí road
metas.note: Most roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Rio Grande do Norte and Pernambuco pole plates
metas.note: This small yellow or orange plate attached onto the pole by thin metal or zip tie is found in Rio Grande do Norte and Pernambuco. This ID is usually much higher up the pole in Pernambuco than in Rio Grande do Norte.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Rio Grande do Sul pavement
metas.note: You can often see pavements in Rio Grande do Sul that have brown tiles but are either jagged and random, or square. This style can sometimes be seen in Santa Catarina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Rolling grassy hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Rural Roraima
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Sugarcane plantations
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of São Paulo, and in the coastal north east states, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Uneven stone road
metas.note:
These uneven but mostly square stone roads are seen in western Rio Grande do Sul and west Santa Catarina. The soil will often be very dark in these regions too.

NOTE: The same roads are seen in the Misiones province of Argentina.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Very tall grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.
